cases.question: What is COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture about?
cases.standalone_question: What is the course content and description for COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture at BCIT?
cases.answer_excerpt:
COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture is a 3.0-credit course that focuses on the design, development, and management of web APIs.

The course covers the following key areas:
*   **RESTful APIs:** You will learn what they are, why they are important, and how to apply REST constraints and best practices.
*   **Core Concepts:** The curriculum explores the relationship between HTTP and REST, the use of HTTP status codes, and the implementation of CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations.
*   **Practical Skills:** You will gain experience in designing simple web services, documenting specifications, implementing error handling, and securing backend API servers.
*   **Technical Implementation:** The course involves working with REST, JSON, and HTTP, as well as applying change management and versioning to your API designs.

This course is part of the Computer Systems Technology (CST) Diploma program. It requires the completion of COMP 1537 and COMP 3522 as prerequisites.

Document 2 [URL: https://www.bcit.ca/outlines/20261088086/]
Document 3 [URL: https://www.bcit.ca/programs/computer-systems-technology-diploma-full-time-5500dipma/]

cases.question: What are the three main topic areas covered in COMP 1113 Applied Mathematics?
cases.standalone_question: What are the three main topic areas covered in COMP 1113 Applied Mathematics?
cases.answer_excerpt:
The three main topic areas covered in COMP 1113 (Applied Mathematics) are:

*   **Boolean algebra and the design of logic circuits:** This includes concepts such as truth tables, canonical forms, and simplifying expressions using mathematical proofs and Karnaugh maps.
*   **Number systems and data representation:** This covers positional number systems and how various data types (numbers, text, and graphics) are represented within a computer, including arithmetic operations in different bases like binary, octal, and hexadecimal.
*   **Functions, linear equations, vectors, and matrices:** This involves solving systems of linear equations using algebraic methods, determinants, and matrices, as well as performing basic matrix operations.

Sources:

cases.question: What are the entrance requirements for the Computer Systems Technology diploma?
cases.standalone_question: What are the entrance requirements for the Computer Systems Technology diploma?
cases.answer_excerpt:
The Computer Systems Technology (CST) diploma is offered as both a full-time program and a Flexible Learning (part-time) program. The entrance requirements differ depending on which version you choose:

### Full-Time CST Diploma
For the full-time program, you may apply for direct entry if you have completed equivalent coursework elsewhere or at BCIT. To pursue this:
*   Email **cstdiploma@bcit.ca** to request a pre-assessment information kit.
*   Submit a completed pre-entry assessment (approved by the program area) along with your online application.
*   You must provide proof of meeting all entrance requirements.

### Flexible Learning (Part-Time) CST Diploma
The Flexible Learning diploma is a laddered credential that requires completion of the Computer Systems Certificate (CSC) first. Requirements include:
*   **Post-secondary education:** You must have completed the Computer Systems Certificate (CSC) program. You may apply if you are currently enrolled in your final term of the CSC.
*   **English language proficiency:** Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent. This requirement is satisfied by completing COMM 110x within the CSC program.
*   **Application:** You must submit proof of meeting these requirements and convert all transcripts to PDF files.

If you are planning your path before applying to the Flexible Learning diploma, you are encouraged to email **cstflex@bcit.ca** for assistance.

Sources:
Document 1 [URL: https://www.bcit.ca/programs/computer-syst
sub_queries: BCIT Computer Systems Technology diploma entrance requirements

cases.question: Am I automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan, and can I opt out?
cases.standalone_question: Am I automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan, and can I opt out?
cases.answer_excerpt:
Whether you are automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan and whether you can opt out depends on your program status:

**1) Automatic Enrollment**
You are automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan if you meet the following criteria:
*   You are a student in a program designated as full-time by BCIT.
*   Your program is at least 16 weeks in length.
*   If you meet these requirements, the health fee is automatically included in your tuition upon registration.

**2) Opting Out**
You have the option to opt out of the plan if you already have comparable extended health and dental coverage through another provider. 
*   **Deadline:** You must submit your opt-out request within 30 days from the start of your program. 
*   **Frequency:** Opt-outs can be processed once per 12-month period. 
*   **Important:** After the 30-day deadline, opt-outs cannot be processed.

If you are unsure of your eligibility, you can contact the BCITSA Health & Dental Plan Office located in building SE2 on the Burnaby campus.

Sources:

cases.question: What overall IELTS score does English Category 1 require, and how much is the commitment fee for international students?
cases.standalone_question: What overall IELTS score does English Category 1 require, and how much is the commitment fee for international students at BCIT?
cases.answer_excerpt:
To meet the English Language Proficiency requirements for a program categorized as Category 1, you must achieve an overall IELTS Academic score of 7.0, with no band score below 6.0.

Regarding the commitment fee for international students:
*   Newly admitted international students are required to pay a $6,000 non-refundable commitment fee to confirm their acceptance into a program.
*   This fee is applied toward your tuition upon registration.
*   If you are accepted into the English for Professional and Academic Success (EPAS) program, you will be instructed to pay a $1,000 non-refundable commitment fee, which is also applied to your tuition.

cases.question: Three quick questions: is peer tutoring free, can I opt out of the BCITSA health and dental plan, and what student residences are on the Burnaby campus?
cases.standalone_question: Is BCIT peer tutoring free, can I opt out of the BCITSA health and dental plan, and what student residences are on the Burnaby campus?
cases.answer_excerpt:
Here are the answers to your questions:

**1) Peer Tutoring Cost**
Yes, peer tutoring is free for all BCIT students. It is available on a drop-in basis, and no advance registration is required. You can check the online schedule for current times and locations.

**2) BCITSA Health and Dental Plan Opt-Out**
Full-time, eligible students in technology, trades, or technical studies programs lasting 16 weeks or longer are automatically covered by the BCITSA Student Health and Dental Plan. If you already have comparable extended health and dental benefits, you may opt out. You must complete the opt-out process within 30 days of your program's start date.

**3) Burnaby Campus Student Housing**
BCIT offers on-campus housing at the Burnaby campus through the following residences:
*   **Tall Timber Student Housing:** Opened in Fall 2025, this facility offers fully self-contained Studio rooms and Connected Single rooms.
*   **Townhouses:** These are legacy units that host 12 students each in private rooms with shared common facilities.
